choice: Represent direct methanol formation CO2+3H2⇌CH3OH+H2O as the productive pathway and lump all non-methanol carbon into CO via RWGS; conserve C/H/O at the plant boundary by reporting CO in purge/offgas.
alternatives: Assume selectivity losses form methane or higher oxygenates
Model detailed catalyst-specific formate/carboxyl elementary steps
Ignore byproducts and scale feed only by methanol selectivity
reason: Across Cu-, In2O3-, Pd/ZnO-, Co- and MoS2-based thermal studies, methanol and CO are the consistently quantified products; elementary mechanisms differ by family and cannot be identified uniformly from reactor performance records, while ignoring CO would violate elemental balances.

choice: Transfer each record through its measured methanol productivity as the catalyst-specific intrinsic activity anchor, corrected by an Arrhenius factor and reactant partial-pressure factor and multiplied by a thermodynamic approach-to-equilibrium term; optimize plant per-pass conversion no higher than the equilibrium conversion and size catalyst from net methanol rate. Apply a cycle-average activity penalty when t_cycle_h is reported and a bounded default life uncertainty otherwise.
alternatives: Use lab conversion directly as plant per-pass conversion
Fit one global Langmuir–Hinshelwood law to all catalyst families
Rank solely by reported STY with no equilibrium or pressure correction
Fit catalyst-family-specific kinetic models despite sparse incompatible records
reason: Reported conversion strongly depends on space velocity and equilibrium, whereas productivity contains catalyst-mass-normalized activity. A common semi-empirical approach-to-equilibrium form enables comparison without claiming a universal elementary mechanism; catalyst-specific parameter fitting is unsupported for many papers.

choice: Use parallel multitubular packed-bed reactors with boiling-water/steam heat removal; optimize reactor temperature, pressure, and per-pass CO2 conversion within catalyst-record transfer and equilibrium limits.
alternatives: Adiabatic quench beds
Slurry bubble-column reactor
Isothermal CSTR
Membrane reactor with in-situ water removal
reason: A cooled fixed bed is compatible with the powdered/pelletized heterogeneous catalyst evidence, controls the strongly exothermic reaction, supports high-pressure recycle operation, and permits catalyst inventory to scale directly from mass-specific productivity without introducing unvalidated slurry mass-transfer parameters.

choice: Cool reactor effluent with feed heat recovery, condense crude methanol/water, use a high-pressure knockout for gas recycle, and purify crude methanol by distillation to 99.7 mol% product; purge a small recycle fraction to prevent CO accumulation.
alternatives: Single flash with crude methanol product
Pressure-swing adsorption of methanol
Membrane recycle separation
Reactive condensation or sorption-enhanced reactor
reason: Methanol and water are condensable while H2/CO2/CO remain predominantly gaseous, making condensation plus recycle physically direct; distillation is required to meet a defined product purity, and purge is necessary because RWGS-derived CO otherwise accumulates.

choice: Battery limit begins with separate gaseous CO2 and H2 at 1 bar and ambient temperature and ends with 99.7 mol% methanol at 5 bar, purge/offgas, and treated aqueous waste; upstream CO2 capture and H2 production are represented only by fixed feed prices, while all on-site compression, synthesis, recycle, purification, heat recovery, utilities and offsites are included.
alternatives: Include electrolysis and CO2 capture plants inside the battery limit
Start with feeds already at synthesis pressure
End at crude methanol without purification
reason: This boundary isolates catalyst-dependent conversion/recycle/separation economics while retaining all process units whose duties change with catalyst performance; upstream production technology is not catalyst-dependent and is consistently charged through feed prices.

choice: Do not impose a universal atomistic descriptor model; use reported catalyst elemental composition only for material cost and use measured reactor productivity/selectivity/stability for performance.
alternatives: Volcano model based on oxygen-vacancy formation energy
Cu surface-area or Cu-Zn interface descriptor across all records
Family-specific DFT microkinetic models
Ignore catalyst composition entirely
reason: The usable dataset spans Cu/Zn/Zr, Pd/ZnO, In2O3-derived, Co- and sulfide families with incompatible reported descriptors. No common atomistic quantity is measured for all records or validated to predict rate and selectivity under plant conditions; forcing one would create unsupported rankings, while composition is still relevant to catalyst replacement cost.
